evals.prompt:
Check this against the two fictional personas supplied for this eval. Here's the draft:

Fictional sample: Our volunteer group used to pass a paper signup sheet around at every meeting. Everyone said an online form would solve the problem, so we tried one for the spring clean-up. People who missed the meeting could sign up, which was nice. But two people still showed up to unlock the shed because nobody had checked who already had a key. We also spent a lot more time following up than I expected. I didn't count the minutes. My take: a form makes it easier to collect names, but somebody still has to turn that list into a plan.

One reader wants evidence for changes in workload. The other wants to know whether to use a form for the next event.
evals.expected_output: Review the two inline personas using the pasted text, flagging the unmeasured follow-up effort and the missing criteria for choosing a form. Record the hash, then end with a synthesis. Stay within persona-fit analysis.
